resources.string: Starts a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so that AI clients such as Claude Desktop or Cursor can drive this device through accessibility, scripting and shell capabilities.
The server is bound to 127.0.0.1 by default. A random access token is generated automatically and is required by every request.
When enabled the server listens on all network interfaces, which lets other devices on the same network reach it. Only turn this on in a network you trust.
Port must be within 1024 to 65535. Restart the server after changing it.

Enabling the MCP server opens a network port that lets a connected AI client tap the screen, read the view hierarchy, run scripts and take screenshots.\n\nThe server is bound to 127.0.0.1 and requires an access token. Do not enable local network access on a network you do not control.

Existing clients will stop working until the new token is configured. Continue?
Port must be an integer within 1024 to 65535.

Controls an Android device through the AutoJs6 accessibility service and script engine. Call dump_ui_tree first to understand the current screen, then use ui_find and ui_action to interact with it. When there is no view hierarchy to query -- games, canvases, video surfaces -- reach for find_image or ocr_recognize instead, and use read_notifications for content that never appears in the view tree at all.
Accessibility service is not connected. Enable the AutoJs6 accessibility service first.

The screen could not be read at the moment nothing matched, so this empty result does not prove the element is absent. The accessibility service is most likely reconnecting. Retry in a moment, and if it keeps failing re-enable the AutoJs6 accessibility service.

The dumped window produced no usable nodes (an empty placeholder root at most). Invisible nodes have already been re-included automatically, so if it is still empty the app does not expose its content to accessibility -- fall back to ocr_recognize, find_image or read_notifications.
No readable window was found. Make sure an app is in the foreground and the AutoJs6 accessibility service is connected.
